question: Money was lent on simple interest. After 12 years, its simple interest becomes (3)/(5) of the money. Find the rate of interest.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest percentage = (3 ÷ 5) × 100 = 60%

We know directly that Total SI% = Rate × Time

60% = Rate × 12

Rate = 60 ÷ 12 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Let the Principal amount be P and the Rate of interest be R% p.a.

⇒ Given Time (T) = 12 years

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) after 12 years = (3 ÷ 5) × P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c83b0ae8cac415066ebd2fb6682632b4c893a8f081ab948cacb5eadbf1765884.png] 

⇒ Formula: Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ (3 ÷ 5) × P = (P × R × 12) ÷ 100

⇒ 3 ÷ 5 = (12 × R) ÷ 100

⇒ R = (3 × 100) ÷ (5 × 12)

⇒ R = 300 ÷ 60

⇒ R = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is strictly calculated only on the principal amount, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal amount as well as the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)². For 3 years, Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (3 + R ÷ 100).

Compound Interest Formula

Amount = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ, where n is the number of years or compounding periods. The Compound Interest is obtained by subtracting the Principal from the Amount (CI = Amount − P).
